**How One Big Beautiful Bill Act Threatens Student Success**
The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), passed in July 2024, threatens student success by imposing significant cuts to federal support programs critical to college students' basic needs and financial stability. Nearly 60% of U.S. college students experience at least one form of basic needs insecurity, including food and housing instability. The bill includes $186 billion in cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), requiring all adults aged 18 to 64 to work at least 20 hours per week to qualify—potentially cutting access for approximately one in four college students who face food insecurity. Experts warn this could disproportionately affect low-income and marginalized students. Additionally, the act caps graduate and professional degree loans at $200,000 and $100,000 respectively and eliminates Grad PLUS loans, which may reduce access to higher education for students at historically Black colleges and minority-serving institutions. These changes could lead to increased reliance on high-interest private loans and reduce enrollment and diversity in graduate programs. Policy leaders, including Bryce McKibben of the Hope Center and Jessica Thompson of the Institute for College Access and Success, express deep concern that these changes will exacerbate financial stress and threaten student persistence and degree completion. A 2025 Student Voice survey found 64% of students did not know whether their college offered emergency aid, and only 12% knew how to apply, underscoring systemic gaps in support infrastructure.
